description: Pure parity matrix: identical normalized fixed inputs in simulate and live modes produce deeply equal canonical lines, explanations, tax, proration, and totals.
Pure parity matrix: hourly inputs cover custom/user-type rates, minimum billable time, rounding, overtime, effective schedules, and partial service periods in both modes.
Pure parity matrix: usage inputs cover flat and tiered pricing, minimums, exact tier boundaries, units, effective schedules, tax, and rounding in both modes.
Pure multi-period parity: bucket allowance, consumption, rollover, expiration/non-compounding, and overage yield equal results and explicit next state in both modes.
Pure parity matrix: recurring product and license quantities cover advance/arrears timing, mixed cadence, proration, effective prices, tax, and boundary dates.
Pure document test: percentage/fixed discounts and positive/negative/one-time adjustments are applied once in canonical order with exact minor-unit totals.
Input guards reject cross-tenant identity, invalid half-open windows, mixed currencies, missing effective prices, and malformed obligations before returning a result.
Production golden suite preserves ordered full-detail results for fixed, hourly, usage, bucket, product/license, mixed-cadence, tax, discount, adjustment, and proration contracts.
DB-backed happy path loads a seeded contract through production and scenario adapters and produces equal canonical calculated documents.
DB-backed successful and failing simulations leave cycles, recurring periods, time/usage links, bucket state, invoices, details, numbering, audits, and outbox/event rows unchanged.
Side-effect spies prove simulation never calls tax provisioning, numbering, persistence, reconciliation, audit, analytics, events, PDF, delivery, or credit services.
DB-backed tenant guard rejects foreign-tenant client, contract, line, service, pricing, profile, location, or tax references without partial result or writes.
Production integration persists a live result with unchanged transaction, charge correlation, recurring linkage, profile split, totals, audit, and post-commit events.
Production idempotency integration proves repeated execution identity or existing invoice creates no duplicate invoice, charge, linkage, number, audit, or event.
Runtime/type boundary rejects persisting a simulate-mode result and accepts a valid live-mode result through the production commit adapter.
Simulator response test verifies displayed lines and period subtotal/tax/total directly map shared results, including explanations and stable keys.
Architecture contract permits direct charge-family imports only inside the shared domain engine and prevents simulator financial helper reintroduction.
Existing EE simulator UI smoke verifies run, multi-period timeline, line explanation, and compare behavior after consolidation.
